newsitem.title: UK: UK Tory Scott loses confidence of local party.
newsitem.headline: UK Tory Scott loses confidence of local party.

text.p: Conservative Member of Parliament Sir Nicholas Scott failed to win a vote of confidence from the executive committee of his party branch on Monday and may have to give way to another candidate in the next general election.

Andrew Dalton, chairman of the Kensington and Chelsea Conservative Association in London, told reporters the committee was "unable to endorse a motion of confidence in Sir Nicholas Scott as their prospective parliamentary candidate".
He will now appeal for backing to a full meeting of the Association at a date still to be set.
Scott, a former minister, was found face down in the road by police after a social event at the Conservative Party conference last month. He denied he was drunk, blaming his condition on painkillers.
Newspapers have speculated that Scott could resign immediately if deselected as Conservative candidate.
That would come as a blow to Prime Minister John Major.

His overall majority in the 651-seat House of Commons was cut to just one on Sunday with the death of Conservative MP Barry Porter, and it could be wiped out completely if Labour wins a forthcoming by-election in Barnsley East, northern England, left vacant by the death of the sitting Labour MP.
